RUST-09-boundary-review-evidence/README..content:
# Review a pointer-and-status boundary

The safe baseline adds at most eight bytes into a u32. Review the supplied
private C-ABI stand-in before replacing that baseline with a checked wrapper.
The starter's public checksum stays entirely safe; its raw bridge is compiled
only for tests. The reference enables the private bridge and contains its raw
values behind the same public `checksum(&[u8]) -> Result<u32, BoundaryError>`.
No public Rust function accepts a raw pointer or a caller-selected backend.

The named need is auditing an existing pointer/length/output/status contract.
The stand-in is implemented in Rust with the C calling convention so it needs
no external library. These tests demonstrate the local ABI call and wrapper;
they do not verify a foreign C build, binary compatibility or an actual vendor
library. For ordinary Rust-only summation, keep `safe_checksum` instead.

## Contract and source map

Read src/lib.rs first, then src/bridge.rs. MAX_BYTES is 8. Each input value is
u8, so the largest accepted sum is 2040, safely representable in u32. Empty
input has sum 0. A ninth byte returns TooLarge before an ABI call. The API
returns an owned number; it neither changes input nor returns or retains a
borrow into it. A slice is borrowed initialized storage; a raw pointer carries
no equivalent checked length or lifetime. An unsafe block records a proof
obligation, not a runtime validation of arbitrary memory.

The supplied ABI shape corresponds to a C prototype such as
`int32_t sum(const uint8_t *data, size_t length, uint32_t *output)`.
Do not substitute a Rust Vec, String, reference or enum as an undocumented C
parameter. Target ABI, size_t and unwind behavior need independent agreement
before a real cross-language integration. This case exports no symbol.

raw_sum returns status 0 only after writing a sum, or 64 without writing.
It first refuses length > 8, null output, or null input with nonzero length.
Null input with length 0 uses an existing empty slice; it is never passed to
from_raw_parts. Null checks cannot establish allocation, alignment, provenance,
initialized bytes, aliasing, synchronization or lifetime for a non-null pointer.
Those remain caller obligations. Do not manufacture dangling or misaligned
callers to test the native boundary.

For a nonempty input, the caller must supply initialized readable bytes within
one live allocation, unchanged during the call. A non-null output must be live,
aligned and writable for one u32, disjoint from the input. The callee must not
retain, free or mutate input, overrun either allocation or unwind across this
ABI. These are contracts to inspect, not properties a pointer type proves.

In the reference, checked_sum chooses only the fixed private raw_sum. invoke
checks length, creates a separate initialized stack output and makes the call
while the input borrow remains live. It maps 64 to Rejected and every unknown
status to Protocol. Status 0 is accepted only if the output is <= length × 255.
The initial u32::MAX sentinel makes a missing write a protocol error without
reading uninitialized storage. A malicious callee could still corrupt memory
before returning; checking status or a plausible sum cannot make that safe.
An in-range wrong sum is a semantic defect, tested against the safe baseline.
No panic is expected from this finite, nonallocating byte loop and bounded sum;
extern C is not an agreement to unwind safely. The test backends are fixed,
private, synchronous stand-ins that obey memory safety while violating status
or output semantics. They model a logic failure, not arbitrary foreign code.

## Unsafe ledger

For each row, identify the operation, guarantee the compiler cannot establish,
caller/callee obligation, supporting safe-code fact, failure behavior, negative
test, Miri observation and residual limitation. Read the code to check each
comment; a SAFETY comment alone is not evidence.

| Operation | Required fact | Safe wrapper fact or test | Remaining obligation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| from_raw_parts in raw_sum | Non-null, initialized, live, single-allocation immutable bytes with a valid length | The wrapper borrows a Rust byte slice and caps length at 8; null empty input takes a separate branch | A different native caller must establish validity; null checks are insufficient |
| output.write in raw_sum | Aligned, live, disjoint writable u32 | The wrapper passes a distinct stack local; guarded failures preserve a sentinel | The callee must respect output bounds and not retain it |
| Calling the unsafe C-ABI function | Compatible signature, all memory preconditions, no retention/free/unwind | Fixed private function pointer, live borrows and checked status/output protocol | A foreign replacement needs a separate audit and link/build evidence |
| Reading the saved pointer in miri-dangling.rs | The allocation would need to remain live | The provided experiment frees it first and must be rejected under Miri | Never infer a native execution is safe because it happens to print 7 |

## Build and predict

Use Rust 1.97.1, edition 2024, Cargo, rustfmt and Clippy. Both roles contain a
complete lockfile and no external crates. From one role directory:

```sh
cargo fmt --all --check
rustfmt --edition 2024 --check diagnostics/*.rs
cargo clippy --locked --offline --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --locked --offline
cargo run --locked --offline -- --help
cargo run --locked --offline -- --case empty
cargo run --locked --offline -- --case valid
cargo run --locked --offline -- --case cap
cargo run --locked --offline -- --case over
cargo build --locked --offline
```

The three successful cases print respectively `length=0 checksum=0`,
`length=2 checksum=24`, and `length=8 checksum=2040`, each with one final
newline, empty stderr and status 0. Over writes only `error=too-large` and a
newline to stderr, status 65. Help prints
`usage: boundary_review_lab --help | --case NAME` and a newline to stdout,
status 0. Missing, unknown, extra or non-UTF-8 arguments print that usage only
to stderr, status 64. Argument collection stops after three items. The CLI
selects four fixed fictional byte vectors and accepts no files or callbacks.
Run cargo clean, then repeat tests and build. Record streams, status, tool
versions and one independently predicted case, not just a passing summary.

## Core, continuation, choice and challenge

CORE: retain the safe baseline and define its observable contract. Audit the
supplied raw_sum before calling it. Complete CORE and LIMITS in observations.md,
including every ledger row, the need for the boundary and a safe alternative.
Add a distinct edge case that is not a copy of the supplied tests.

WORKFLOW: continue the same project. Implement a checked public checksum over
the private ABI while preserving the baseline contract. Keep raw pointers
inside the bridge; establish bounds, borrows, output lifetime and status
handling. Record exact-cap and one-over results and a clean rebuild. Explain
why checking a result after the call cannot undo an invalid callee write.

CHOICE: extend the private protocol seam with one deterministic, memory-safe
bad-status or bad-output backend. Test refusal, an unknown status, a missing
write, an impossible output and an in-range incorrect sum. State which are
detected by the wrapper and which need the independent baseline comparison.
Do not use an arbitrary caller-selected function pointer or real library.

CHALLENGE: compile unsafe-call.rs and unsafe-body.rs separately with
`rustc --edition=2024 diagnostics/NAME.rs -o NAME`; both must be refused with
E0133. explicit-call.rs and explicit-body.rs compile and print 7. Explain the
separate obligations of an unsafe function and its inner operations. Review
the supplied Miri experiment and recorded evidence below. Running Miri is
optional; never run miri-dangling.rs natively. A clean finite Miri run is not a
proof of every input, target, schedule, foreign implementation or ABI.

## Miri experiment

The CI experiment uses nightly-2026-07-16 with its Miri and rust-src components.
Toolchain and sysroot setup is separate from offline project checks. The
interpreter runs both roles' library tests, then the single supplied dangling
case in an isolated generated Cargo harness, with process timeouts. It must
accept the valid library tests and reject the freed-allocation read. No real
foreign library, network program or unbounded fuzzer is involved. The rejected
program is interpreted only under Miri; its observed value is never treated
as a valid ordinary result. Keep its source hash and actual diagnostic together.

## Recorded interpreter evidence

This record comes from [the pinned source revision](https://github.com/instruction-material/Low-Level-Security/tree/ebf8c6d1b8cab2604a87e0f464862223e89a526a/RUST-09-boundary-review-evidence)
and [its CI run](https://github.com/instruction-material/Low-Level-Security/actions/runs/39129421999).
The interpreter used `miri 0.1.0 (d0babd8b6b 2026-07-15)` with
`rustc 1.99.0-nightly (d0babd8b6 2026-07-15)` and `-Zmiri-strict-provenance`.
The starter's 11 library tests and the reference's 17 library tests passed.
The single rejected case returned status 1 with empty stdout.

The generated harness used the exact bytes of `diagnostics/miri-dangling.rs`
as `src/main.rs`. Its source SHA-256 is
`2a86f76a805aff61ee51c0cf6a819f331bc508c45d2cc1e9ade9556b744cafb7`; the full diagnostic SHA-256 is
`2f7f729223fb1c81f14fbcf8aa295e1360b4643af1fcf0f191ec443e8189a66e`. The excerpt retains the recorded
allocation identifier and shows the allocation, deallocation and invalid read:

```text
error: Undefined Behavior: memory access failed: alloc236 has been freed, so this pointer is dangling
 --> src/main.rs:7:29
  |
7 |     let observed = unsafe { *saved };
  |                             ^^^^^^ Undefined Behavior occurred here
  |
  = help: this indicates a bug in the program: it performed an invalid operation, and caused Undefined Behavior
  = help: see https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/behavior-considered-undefined.html for further information
help: alloc236 was allocated here:
 --> src/main.rs:3:31
  |
3 |     let saved = Box::into_raw(Box::new(7_u8));
  |                               ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
help: alloc236 was deallocated here:
 --> src/main.rs:5:14
  |
5 |     unsafe { drop(Box::from_raw(saved)) };
  |              ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
```

The Box was reconstructed and freed once; the later raw-pointer read violates
its lifetime requirement. Compare this interpreter refusal with the two E0133
compile-time refusals. They answer different questions about the same trust
boundary. This finite record does not certify a foreign implementation or
unexamined executions.

References: [Rust Book unsafe Rust](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch20-01-unsafe-rust.html),
[slice contract](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/slice/fn.from_raw_parts.html),
[FFI and unwinding](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nomicon/ffi.html),
[Miri capabilities and limits](https://github.com/rust-lang/miri).

# Boundary review evidence

## CORE
Record the safe contract, a distinct edge case and the named need for the boundary.
Audit every unsafe-ledger row before changing the public checksum.

## WORKFLOW
Record the wrapper's validation, pointer lifetimes, aliasing, output and status
contract. Retain exact streams/statuses and the clean rebuild.

## CHOICE
Add one deterministic memory-safe protocol seam and distinguish runtime protocol
checks from semantic equality and memory-safety obligations.

## CHALLENGE
Record both E0133 refusals and checked alternatives. Read the supplied Miri trace
or retain an actual bounded run with its compiler, source identity and limitations.

## LIMITS
Explain why comments, null checks, plausible outputs and finite dynamic tests
cannot certify arbitrary native pointers, foreign libraries or every execution.

# This file is automatically @generated by Cargo.
# It is not intended for manual editing.
version = 4

[[package]]
name = "boundary_review_lab"
version = "1.0.0"

# Reference boundary review

## CORE
The safe oracle caps input at eight bytes. Empty sums to zero; [7,17] sums to 24;
eight 255 bytes sum to 2040. A ninth byte is rejected before pointer conversion.
The local ABI is supplied for contract review; pure Rust summation needs no FFI.
Source pointers and output pointers remain inside the private bridge.

## WORKFLOW
The input slice remains borrowed through the call and the output is a distinct
initialized u32 local. The fixed raw_sum must not retain, free or mutate input,
overrun output or unwind. Nonempty slice construction depends on the live,
initialized, single-allocation input contract. Empty input avoids a null slice.
Null refusal tests are guarded paths, not validation of arbitrary non-null
addresses. The reference maps status 64 to Rejected and unknown statuses to
Protocol. Missing writes and impossible sums are caught by the initialized
sentinel and range check. Retain actual commands and a separate regression.

## CHOICE
The private test seam returns defined refusal, unknown status, success without
writing, and success with 2041. It obeys memory-safety obligations while violating
the logical protocol. A plausible wrong sum would pass the range check, so
compare it with safe_checksum. A malicious write could cause UB before any
status check; this reference does not claim to contain an arbitrary callee.

## CHALLENGE
E0133 distinguishes calling an unsafe function without a block from performing
an unchecked operation inside an unsafe function under deny(unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn).
Both explicit alternatives retain the same live-byte precondition. The Miri-only
case reconstructs and drops its Box exactly once, then deliberately reads the
freed allocation. Use the recorded Miri evidence in README or run the bounded
experiment; never treat a native value from that case as valid evidence.

## LIMITS
This is a local Rust implementation of a C ABI, not a tested foreign C library.
No raw pointer, backend selection or exported symbol is exposed by the public
Rust API. The compiler checks types; the ledger, independent corpus and Miri
evidence address different contracts and do not prove every target or execution.

test/verify_rust_boundary.py.content:
"""Compile RSS9 roles and retain exact native contract evidence."""
import argparse
import datetime
import hashlib
import itertools
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import signal
import subprocess
import tempfile
import time
import tomllib

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
PACK = ROOT / "RUST-09-boundary-review-evidence"
parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
parser.add_argument("--proof", type=Path, required=True)
parser.add_argument("--source-kind", choices=["checkout","exported-workspace"], default="checkout")
args = parser.parse_args()
args.proof = args.proof.resolve()
assert not args.proof.exists()
assert os.getuid() != 0 and os.uname().sysname == "Linux" and os.uname().machine == "x86_64"
OUT = args.proof.parent
OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
commands = []


def sha(raw):
    return hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()


def stop(signum, _frame):
    raise SystemExit(128 + signum)


signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, stop)
signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, stop)


def run(command, cwd, label, expected=0, env=None, timeout=120):
    entry = dict(parentTaskId="rust-boundary-evidence", parentPid=os.getpid(),
                 command=[os.fsdecode(value) for value in command], cwd=str(cwd),
                 startTime=datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC).isoformat(), timeoutSeconds=timeout)
    start = time.monotonic()
    child = subprocess.Popen(command, cwd=cwd, env=env, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                             stderr=subprocess.PIPE, start_new_session=True)
    entry["pid"] = child.pid
    with (OUT / "processes.jsonl").open("a") as stream:
        stream.write(json.dumps(dict(entry, event="start")) + "\n")
    stdout, stderr, cleanup = b"", b"", "owned process exited"
    try:
        stdout, stderr = child.communicate(timeout=timeout)
    except BaseException:
        if child.poll() is None:
            os.killpg(child.pid, signal.SIGTERM)
            try:
                stdout, stderr = child.communicate(timeout=3)
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                os.killpg(child.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
                stdout, stderr = child.communicate()
        cleanup = "owned process group terminated and reaped"
        raise
    finally:
        with (OUT / "processes.jsonl").open("a") as stream:
            stream.write(json.dumps(dict(entry, event="end", endTime=datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC).isoformat(),
                                         exitCode=child.returncode, childProcessGroupCleanup=cleanup)) + "\n")
        (OUT / (label + ".stdout.txt")).write_bytes(stdout)
        (OUT / (label + ".stderr.txt")).write_bytes(stderr)
    assert child.returncode == expected, (label, child.returncode, stderr.decode(errors="replace"))
    commands.append(dict(label=label, exitCode=child.returncode, elapsedSeconds=time.monotonic()-start,
                         timeoutSeconds=timeout, stdoutSha256=sha(stdout), stderrSha256=sha(stderr)))
    return stdout, stderr


def verify_committed_bytes(actual, source):
    # Compare raw bytes with the selected commit, independently of the index,
    # clean filters, timestamps, and assume-unchanged flags.
    listing=run(["git","ls-tree","-rz","--full-tree",actual,"--",*source],ROOT,"committed-source-objects")[0]
    entries={}
    for row in listing.split(b"\0"):
        if not row:
            continue
        header,name=row.split(b"\t",1)
        mode,kind,identity=header.split()
        assert mode in [b"100644",b"100755"] and kind==b"blob"
        name=name.decode()
        assert name not in entries
        entries[name]=identity.decode()
    assert entries.keys()==source.keys(),"Committed source paths differ"
    for name,raw in source.items():
        identity=hashlib.sha1(b"blob "+str(len(raw)).encode()+b"\0"+raw).hexdigest()
        assert identity==entries[name],"Source bytes differ from committed revision: "+name
    return entries


claimed=os.environ["SOURCE_REVISION"]
role_names=["Cargo.toml","Cargo.lock","src/lib.rs","src/main.rs","src/bridge.rs","observations.md",
            "diagnostics/unsafe-call.rs","diagnostics/explicit-call.rs","diagnostics/unsafe-body.rs",
            "diagnostics/explicit-body.rs","diagnostics/miri-dangling.rs"]
expected_names=sorted([PACK.name+"/README.md"]+
                      [PACK.name+"/"+role+"/"+name for role in ["starter","solution"] for name in role_names]+
                      ["test/verify_rust_boundary.py","test/verify_rust_boundary_miri.py",
                       "test/verify_rust_boundary_export.py",".github/workflows/rust-boundary.yml"])
assert len(expected_names)==27
actual=None
if args.source_kind=="checkout":
    actual=run(["git","rev-parse","HEAD"],ROOT,"actual-source-revision")[0].decode().strip()
    assert actual==claimed,"Checked-out revision differs from claimed source"
    source_names=run(["git","ls-files","--",PACK.name,"test/verify_rust_boundary.py","test/verify_rust_boundary_miri.py","test/verify_rust_boundary_export.py",".github/workflows/rust-boundary.yml"],ROOT,"source-inventory")[0].decode().splitlines()
    assert source_names==expected_names
else:
    source_names=expected_names
# Every selected path and its in-root ancestors must be regular, non-link input.
for name in source_names:
    cursor=ROOT
    for part in Path(name).parts:
        cursor=cursor/part
        assert not cursor.is_symlink(),"Linked source entry: "+name
    assert cursor.is_file(),"Missing source entry: "+name
# Reject extra package entries without descending into unknown/generated trees.
package_files={name.removeprefix(PACK.name+"/") for name in expected_names if name.startswith(PACK.name+"/")}
package_dirs={Path(".")}
for name in package_files:
    package_dirs.update(Path(name).parents)
for relative in package_dirs:
    directory=PACK/relative
    expected_children={Path(name).parts[len(relative.parts) if str(relative)!="." else 0] for name in package_files
                       if Path(name).is_relative_to(relative) and len(Path(name).parts)>(len(relative.parts) if str(relative)!="." else 0)}
    assert {path.name for path in directory.iterdir()}==expected_children,"Unexpected package entry: "+str(relative)
source={name:(ROOT/name).read_bytes() for name in source_names}
committed_objects=verify_committed_bytes(actual,source) if args.source_kind=="checkout" else None
assert all(b"\r" not in raw for raw in source.values())
for name,raw in source.items():
    target=OUT/"source"/name
    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
    target.write_bytes(raw)
versions={name:run(command,ROOT,name)[0].decode().strip() for name,command in [
    ("rustc",["rustc","--version","--verbose"]),("cargo",["cargo","--version"]),
    ("rustfmt",["rustfmt","--version"]),("clippy",["cargo","clippy","--version"]) ]}
assert versions["rustc"].startswith("rustc 1.97.1 ")
USAGE=b"usage: boundary_review_lab --help | --case NAME\n"
cases={"empty":(b"length=0 checksum=0\n",b"",0),"valid":(b"length=2 checksum=24\n",b"",0),
       "cap":(b"length=8 checksum=2040\n",b"",0),"over":(b"",b"error=too-large\n",65)}
usage=[[],["--case"],["--help","extra"],["--case","valid","extra"],["--case","valid","extra","more"],["--unknown"],["valid"],["--case","unknown"]]
corpus=[list(values) for length in range(5) for values in itertools.product([0,1,255],repeat=length)]
corpus.extend([([value]*length) for length in range(5,10) for value in [0,1,255]])
assert len(corpus)==136
consumer=["use boundary_review_lab::{checksum, safe_checksum};", "fn show(value: Result<u32,boundary_review_lab::BoundaryError>) -> String { match value { Ok(n)=>format!(\"ok:{n}\"), Err(error)=>format!(\"error:{}\",error.code()) } }", "fn main() {"]
for index,values in enumerate(corpus):
    literal=",".join(map(str,values))
    consumer.append(f'let bytes: &[u8]=&[{literal}]; println!("case={index} checksum={{}} safe={{}}",show(checksum(bytes)),show(safe_checksum(bytes)));')
consumer.append("}")
roles=[]
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="rust-boundary-native-") as directory:
    work=Path(directory)
    for role,unit_tests in [("starter",11),("solution",17)]:
        selected=PACK/role
        project=work/role
        shutil.copytree(selected,project)
        original={p.relative_to(selected):p.read_bytes() for p in selected.rglob("*") if p.is_file()}
        lock=(project/"Cargo.lock").read_bytes()
        assert tomllib.loads((project/"Cargo.toml").read_text())=={"package":{"name":"boundary_review_lab","version":"1.0.0","edition":"2024"}}
        assert tomllib.loads(lock.decode())["package"]==[{"name":"boundary_review_lab","version":"1.0.0"}]
        env={**os.environ,"CARGO_TARGET_DIR":str(work/(role+"-target")),"CARGO_NET_OFFLINE":"true"}
        run(["cargo","fmt","--all","--check"],project,role+"-format",env=env)
        diagnostics=sorted((project/"diagnostics").glob("*.rs"))
        assert len(diagnostics)==5
        run(["rustfmt","--edition","2024","--check",*map(str,diagnostics)],project,role+"-diagnostic-format",env=env)
        run(["cargo","clippy","--locked","--offline","--all-targets","--","-D","warnings"],project,role+"-clippy",env=env)
        assert f"{unit_tests} passed; 0 failed".encode() in run(["cargo","test","--locked","--offline"],project,role+"-tests",env=env)[0]
        run(["cargo","build","--locked","--offline"],project,role+"-build",env=env)
        binary=Path(env["CARGO_TARGET_DIR"])/"debug/boundary_review_lab"
        assert run([str(binary),"--help"],work,role+"-help",env=env,timeout=30)==(USAGE,b"")
        for repeat in range(3):
            for case,expected in cases.items():
                assert run([str(binary),"--case",case],work,f"{role}-case-{case}-{repeat}",expected=expected[2],env=env,timeout=30)==expected[:2]
        for index,arguments in enumerate(usage):
            assert run([str(binary),*arguments],work,f"{role}-usage-{index}",expected=64,env=env,timeout=30)==(b"",USAGE)
        for index,arguments in enumerate([[b"--case",b"\xff"],[b"\xff"]]):
            assert run([os.fsencode(binary),*arguments],work,f"{role}-utf8-{index}",expected=64,env=env,timeout=30)==(b"",USAGE)
        for diagnostic in diagnostics:
            if diagnostic.name=="miri-dangling.rs":
                continue
            rejected=diagnostic.stem in {"unsafe-call","unsafe-body"}
            target=work/(role+"-"+diagnostic.stem)
            out,err=run(["rustc","--edition=2024","--error-format=json",str(diagnostic),"-o",str(target)],work,role+"-"+diagnostic.stem+"-compile",expected=int(rejected),env=env)
            assert out==b""
            if rejected:
                messages=[json.loads(line) for line in err.splitlines()]
                assert any(isinstance(message.get("code"),dict) and message["code"]["code"]=="E0133" for message in messages)
                assert not target.exists()
            else:
                assert err==b""
                assert run([str(target)],work,role+"-"+diagnostic.stem+"-run",env=env,timeout=30)==(b"7\n",b"")
        probe=work/(role+"-consumer.rs")
        probe.write_text("\n".join(consumer)+"\n")
        executable=work/(role+"-consumer")
        run(["rustc","--edition=2024","--crate-name","consumer",str(probe),"--extern","boundary_review_lab="+str(Path(env["CARGO_TARGET_DIR"])/"debug/libboundary_review_lab.rlib"),"-L","dependency="+str(Path(env["CARGO_TARGET_DIR"])/"debug/deps"),"-o",str(executable)],work,role+"-consumer-compile",env=env)
        out,err=run([str(executable)],work,role+"-consumer-run",env=env,timeout=30)
        assert err==b""
        expected=[]
        for index,values in enumerate(corpus):
            result="error:too-large" if len(values)>8 else "ok:"+str(sum(values))
            expected.append(f"case={index} checksum={result} safe={result}")
        assert out.decode().splitlines()==expected
        run(["cargo","clean"],project,role+"-clean",env=env)
        assert not binary.exists()
        assert f"{unit_tests} passed; 0 failed".encode() in run(["cargo","test","--locked","--offline"],project,role+"-clean-tests",env=env)[0]
        run(["cargo","build","--locked","--offline"],project,role+"-clean-build",env=env)
        assert run([str(binary),"--case","valid"],work,role+"-clean-valid",env=env,timeout=30)==cases["valid"][:2]
        assert {p.relative_to(project):p.read_bytes() for p in project.rglob("*") if p.is_file()}==original
        saved=OUT/role
        saved.mkdir()
        shutil.copyfile(binary,saved/"boundary_review_lab")
        roles.append(dict(role=role,unitTests=unit_tests,unitTestsBeforeAndAfterClean=True,sourceAndLockUnchanged=True,
                          consumerCases=len(corpus),apiResults=len(corpus)*2,cliCases=12,usageRefusals=10,
                          compilerRefusals=2,consumerRows=expected,executableSha256=sha(binary.read_bytes())))

"""Interpret RSS9 library tests and the single supplied rejected case."""
import argparse
import datetime
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import signal
import subprocess
import tempfile
import time
import tomllib

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
PACK = ROOT / "RUST-09-boundary-review-evidence"
parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
parser.add_argument("--proof", type=Path, required=True)
args = parser.parse_args()
args.proof = args.proof.resolve()
assert not args.proof.exists()
assert os.getuid() != 0 and os.uname().sysname == "Linux" and os.uname().machine == "x86_64"
OUT = args.proof.parent
OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
commands = []


def sha(raw):
    return hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()


def stop(signum, _frame):
    raise SystemExit(128 + signum)


signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, stop)
signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, stop)


def run(command, cwd, label, expected=0, env=None, timeout=120):
    entry = dict(parentTaskId="rust-boundary-miri-evidence", parentPid=os.getpid(),
                 command=[os.fsdecode(value) for value in command], cwd=str(cwd),
                 startTime=datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC).isoformat(), timeoutSeconds=timeout)
    start = time.monotonic()
    child = subprocess.Popen(command, cwd=cwd, env=env, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                             stderr=subprocess.PIPE, start_new_session=True)
    entry["pid"] = child.pid
    with (OUT / "processes.jsonl").open("a") as stream:
        stream.write(json.dumps(dict(entry, event="start")) + "\n")
    stdout, stderr, cleanup = b"", b"", "owned process exited"
    try:
        stdout, stderr = child.communicate(timeout=timeout)
    except BaseException:
        if child.poll() is None:
            os.killpg(child.pid, signal.SIGTERM)
            try:
                stdout, stderr = child.communicate(timeout=3)
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                os.killpg(child.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
                stdout, stderr = child.communicate()
        cleanup = "owned process group terminated and reaped"
        raise
    finally:
        with (OUT / "processes.jsonl").open("a") as stream:
            stream.write(json.dumps(dict(entry, event="end", endTime=datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC).isoformat(),
                                         exitCode=child.returncode, childProcessGroupCleanup=cleanup)) + "\n")
        (OUT / (label + ".stdout.txt")).write_bytes(stdout)
        (OUT / (label + ".stderr.txt")).write_bytes(stderr)
    assert child.returncode == expected, (label, child.returncode, stderr.decode(errors="replace"))
    commands.append(dict(label=label, exitCode=child.returncode, elapsedSeconds=time.monotonic()-start,
                         timeoutSeconds=timeout, stdoutSha256=sha(stdout), stderrSha256=sha(stderr)))
    return stdout, stderr

    # clean filters, timestamps, and assume-unchanged flags.
    listing=run(["git","ls-tree","-rz","--full-tree",actual,"--",*source],ROOT,"committed-source-objects")[0]
    entries={}
    for row in listing.split(b"\0"):
        if not row:
            continue
        header,name=row.split(b"\t",1)
        mode,kind,identity=header.split()
        assert mode in [b"100644",b"100755"] and kind==b"blob"
        name=name.decode()
        assert name not in entries
        entries[name]=identity.decode()
    assert entries.keys()==source.keys(),"Committed source paths differ"
    for name,raw in source.items():
        identity=hashlib.sha1(b"blob "+str(len(raw)).encode()+b"\0"+raw).hexdigest()
        assert identity==entries[name],"Source bytes differ from committed revision: "+name
    return entries


NIGHTLY="nightly-2026-07-16"
claimed=os.environ["SOURCE_REVISION"]
actual=run(["git","rev-parse","HEAD"],ROOT,"actual-source-revision")[0].decode().strip()
assert actual==claimed
source_names=run(["git","ls-files","--",PACK.name,"test/verify_rust_boundary.py","test/verify_rust_boundary_miri.py","test/verify_rust_boundary_export.py",".github/workflows/rust-boundary.yml"],ROOT,"source-inventory")[0].decode().splitlines()
assert len(source_names)==len(set(source_names))==27
source={name:(ROOT/name).read_bytes() for name in source_names}
committed_objects=verify_committed_bytes(actual,source)
for name,raw in source.items():
    target=OUT/"source"/name
    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
    target.write_bytes(raw)
versions={name:run(command,ROOT,name)[0].decode().strip() for name,command in [
    ("rustc-nightly",["rustc","+"+NIGHTLY,"--version","--verbose"]),
    ("cargo-nightly",["cargo","+"+NIGHTLY,"--version"]),
    ("miri",["cargo","+"+NIGHTLY,"miri","--version"]) ]}
assert "nightly" in versions["rustc-nightly"] and versions["miri"].startswith("miri ")
roles=[]
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="rust-boundary-miri-") as directory:
    work=Path(directory)
    for role,count in [("starter",11),("solution",17)]:
        selected=PACK/role
        project=work/role
        shutil.copytree(selected,project)
        original={p.relative_to(selected):p.read_bytes() for p in selected.rglob("*") if p.is_file()}
        env={**os.environ,"CARGO_TARGET_DIR":str(work/(role+"-miri-target")),"CARGO_NET_OFFLINE":"true","MIRIFLAGS":"-Zmiri-strict-provenance"}
        out,_=run(["cargo","+"+NIGHTLY,"miri","test","--locked","--offline","--lib"],project,role+"-miri-tests",env=env,timeout=180)
        assert f"{count} passed; 0 failed".encode() in out
        assert {p.relative_to(project):p.read_bytes() for p in project.rglob("*") if p.is_file()}==original
        roles.append(dict(role=role,unitTests=count,libraryTestsPassed=True,sourceAndLockUnchanged=True))
    bad=source[PACK.name+"/starter/diagnostics/miri-dangling.rs"]
    assert bad==source[PACK.name+"/solution/diagnostics/miri-dangling.rs"]
    project=work/"rejected"
    (project/"src").mkdir(parents=True)
    toml=b'[package]\nname = "boundary_miri_negative"\nversion = "1.0.0"\nedition = "2024"\n'
    lock=b'# This file is automatically @generated by Cargo.\n# It is not intended for manual editing.\nversion = 4\n\n[[package]]\nname = "boundary_miri_negative"\nversion = "1.0.0"\n'
    driver={"Cargo.toml":toml,"Cargo.lock":lock,"src/main.rs":bad}
    for name,raw in driver.items():
        (project/name).write_bytes(raw)
        target=OUT/"generated-driver"/name
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
        target.write_bytes(raw)
    env={**os.environ,"CARGO_TARGET_DIR":str(work/"negative-miri-target"),"CARGO_NET_OFFLINE":"true","MIRIFLAGS":"-Zmiri-strict-provenance"}
    out,err=run(["cargo","+"+NIGHTLY,"miri","run","--locked","--offline"],project,"miri-rejected-dangling",expected=1,env=env,timeout=180)
    assert out==b"" and b"Undefined Behavior" in err and b"freed" in err
    assert {p.relative_to(project):p.read_bytes() for p in project.rglob("*") if p.is_file()}=={Path(name):raw for name,raw in driver.items()}
assert not work.exists() and all((ROOT/name).read_bytes()==raw for name,raw in source.items())
assert len(commands)==9
proof=dict(committedSourceObjects=committed_objects,sourceRevision=actual,checkedOutRevision=actual,sourceKind="checkout",nightly=NIGHTLY,
           compilerVersions=versions,miriExecuted=True,ordinaryUser=True,
           sourceFiles={name:sha(raw) for name,raw in source.items()},allSourceFilesUnchanged=True,
           temporarySourceCleanup=True,projectChecksOffline=True,
           toolchainAndSysrootSetupSeparate=True,noExternalProjectCrates=True,
           strictProvenanceFlag="-Zmiri-strict-provenance",roles=roles,
           rejectedCase=dict(sourcePath=PACK.name+"/starter/diagnostics/miri-dangling.rs",sourceSha256=sha(bad),
                             generatedDriver={name:sha(raw) for name,raw in driver.items()},
                             expectedStatus=1,actualStatus=1,undefinedBehaviorDetected=True,
                             freedAllocationDiagnostic=True,nativeExecution=False),
           worksheetCompletionNotInferred=True,allInputsTargetsAndForeignLibrariesNotProven=True,
           commands=commands)
args.proof.write_text(json.dumps(proof,indent=2)+"\n")
print(json.dumps({"accepted":True,"commands":9,"miriUnitResults":28,"expectedUBRefusals":1,"proof":str(args.proof)}))

.github/workflows/rust-boundary.yml.content:
name: Rust boundary review evidence

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "RUST-09-boundary-review-evidence/**"
      - "test/verify_rust_boundary.py"
      - "test/verify_rust_boundary_miri.py"
      - "test/verify_rust_boundary_export.py"
      - ".github/workflows/rust-boundary.yml"
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "RUST-09-boundary-review-evidence/**"
      - "test/verify_rust_boundary.py"
      - "test/verify_rust_boundary_miri.py"
      - "test/verify_rust_boundary_export.py"
      - ".github/workflows/rust-boundary.yml"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 20
    env:
      RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: "1.97.1"
      SOURCE_REVISION: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Install the recorded native course toolchain
        run: rustup toolchain install 1.97.1 --profile minimal --component rustfmt --component clippy
      - name: Verify safe baseline, ABI contracts and exact native results
        run: python3 test/verify_rust_boundary.py --source-kind checkout --proof output/rust-boundary-native/proof.json
      - name: Retain formatter suggestions after a failed native validation
        if: failure()
        run: |
          for role in starter solution; do
            for path in src/lib.rs src/main.rs src/bridge.rs 'diagnostics/*.rs'; do
              for source in RUST-09-boundary-review-evidence/"$role"/$path; do
                relative="${source#RUST-09-boundary-review-evidence/}"
                destination="output/rust-boundary-native/formatting/$relative"
                mkdir -p "$(dirname "$destination")"
                rustfmt --edition 2024 --emit stdout "$source" > "$destination"
              done
            done
          done
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a
        if: always()
        with:
          name: rust-boundary-native-evidence
          path: output/rust-boundary-native/
          include-hidden-files: true
          if-no-files-found: error
      - name: Verify a plain exported source packet without Git
        run: python3 test/verify_rust_boundary_export.py --proof output/rust-boundary-exported/proof.json
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a
        if: always()
        with:
          name: rust-boundary-exported-evidence
          path: output/rust-boundary-exported/
          include-hidden-files: true
          if-no-files-found: warn
      - name: Install the recorded optional interpreter toolchain
        run: rustup toolchain install nightly-2026-07-16 --profile minimal --component miri --component rust-src
      - name: Prepare the Miri sysroot before offline project checks
        run: cargo +nightly-2026-07-16 miri setup
      - name: Check valid library tests and the supplied Miri-only rejected case
        run: python3 test/verify_rust_boundary_miri.py --proof output/rust-boundary-miri/proof.json
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a
        if: always()
        with:
          name: rust-boundary-miri-evidence
          path: output/rust-boundary-miri/
          include-hidden-files: true
          if-no-files-found: warn
